intro: Section 32.2 follows adult development from about 20 to 65: the transition from adolescence and the tasks of young adulthood, work identity and unemployment, friendship, sexuality and marriage (including interracial and same-sex marriage and couples therapy), parenthood, single-parent and adoptive families, the move into middle adulthood with the theories of Erikson, Vaillant, and Colarusso and Nemiroff, midlife friendships, relationships and sexuality, the climacterium, midlife transition and crisis, the empty nest, divorce with its types and custody arrangements, and adult maturity. US figures and law are as the book gives them. Update boxes add Obergefell and the Respect for Marriage Act, a correction on Loving v. Virginia, the status of divorce law in the Philippines, and Tan-Andal v. Andal (2021) on psychological incapacity.
objectives: Describe the developmental tasks of young adulthood and the concepts used to describe adult development (Tables 32-15 and 32-16).
Explain how work, unemployment, friendship, marriage and parenthood shape adult identity, and when couples therapy fits.
Compare the main theories of middle adulthood (Erikson, Vaillant, Colarusso and Nemiroff, Levinson) and the features of midlife (Table 32-17).
Distinguish a normal midlife transition, the empty nest and the climacterium from a true midlife crisis or disorder.
Name the types of separation in divorce, the custody arrangements and their effects, and describe adult maturity.
